title: Value-free not-all-equal never fails on k-regular systems for k >= 4
claim: For every k >= 4, signed not-all-equal never fails on k-regular k-uniform systems (any signs on incidences). (i) Signed Seymour lemma: if a signed system is not-all-equal-unsatisfiable and minimal, then it has at least as many lines as points, and with equality every real matrix with its signed incidence pattern is nonsingular (sign-nonsingular): otherwise a nonzero real kernel vector colours its support by sign, satisfying every line it meets, and minimality colours the rest. (ii) In a k-regular k-uniform system a minimal failing subsystem has as many lines as points and full degrees, so it is a union of components. (iii) Its incidence pattern is not sign-nonsingular: with a perfect matching as diagonal its digraph has in- and out-degree k - 1 >= 3, every weak component of a regular digraph is strong, and Thomassen (1992) proved such digraphs even (an even-weight cycle under every 0/1 weighting). At k = 3 the digraph has degree 2 and the failures are exactly the knot's Pfaffian spaces. Checked: k = 4, every 4-regular 4-uniform system with n <= 7 and every signing satisfiable; no such incidence graph has a sign-nonsingular signing; not-all-equal pieces with up to five internal points accept only not-all-equal relations or everything.
failure_conditions: A signed k-regular k-uniform system (k >= 4) with no not-all-equal solution.
A 4-regular bipartite graph with a sign-nonsingular signing.
A minimal failing signed system with fewer lines than points.
foundation_claim_scope: A satisfiability theorem for one value-free law on regular systems; inherits Thomassen's even-digraph theorem.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-31.
validation.status: checked: exhaustive satisfiability over every signing of every 4-regular 4-uniform system with n <= 7; no sign-nonsingular signing of their incidence graphs; digraph degrees; the lemma's cubic instance (PINNING C: failing iff Pfaffian, 1,380,864 signings); rigidity of small pieces; no human or external review
validation.novelty: The plain case is Thomassen (1992) (k >= 4; Alon-Bregman for k >= 8). The signed case follows from Thomassen's even-digraph theorem by Seymour's (1974) linear-algebra argument; no explicit statement was found in the sources checked (moderate folklore risk).
